requirements.title: Nonextended component order follows component declarations
requirements.definition: The component order of a nonextended type follows the order in which its components are declared in the type definition. This is the source-defined ordering used by the named consumers, not a numerical ordering, parameter order, address order or portable physical-layout claim.

requirements.title: Extended component order preserves the inherited prefix and excludes parent components
requirements.source: 7.5.4.7, p1.parent-components-excluded, p2.extended-parent-order-prefix, p2.extended-local-declaration-suffix; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 98.
requirements.definition: An extended type uses its parent type component order first, then its additional components in their declaration order. Parent components themselves do not participate in this ordering; inherited nonparent components do. The definition applies recursively and does not duplicate inherited data by adding a parent component as an extra positional value.

requirements.oracle: A finite flat payload makes duplication, omission and prefix/suffix errors observable without assuming an object layout. All consumer preconditions must be true for the actual extended object.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Nonparent component order and the accessible named parent component are different relations. Parent/ancestor constructor values require keywords, and constructor constraints prevent double specification of inherited data.
